ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The vertical cross-section of a fixed device is shown in the figure, consisting of a smooth straight track $AB$ with an inclination angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$, a smooth circular track $BCD$ with radius $R{=}1\mathrm{m}$, a straight track $DE$ with length $L{=}1.25\mathrm{m}$, inclination angle $\theta$, and kinetic friction coefficient $\mu_{1}{=}0.75$, and a smooth circular pipe $EF$ with radius $R$ and central angle $\theta$. The tracks are smoothly connected. On the smooth horizontal surface to the right of the track end $F$, a slider $^b$ with mass $m{=}0.5\mathrm{kg}$ is placed, with its upper surface aligned with the horizontal plane at the end $F$ of the track. A small block $a$ with mass $m{=}0.5\mathrm{kg}$ is released from rest at a height $h{=}0.8\mathrm{m}$ on track $AB$ and slides through the circular track $BCD$ onto track $DE$. The small block $a$ can be treated as a point mass. Air resistance is negligible, gravitational acceleration $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

1. What is the magnitude of the normal force exerted by the track on the small block when it passes point $C$?
2. What is the total distance \( s \) traveled by the small block \( a \) on \( DE \)?
3. If $h=2.15\mathrm{m}$ and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the small block $a$ and the slider $b$ is $\mu_{2}=0.25$, how long must the slider be to prevent the small block from falling off? (The small block $a$ can undergo a perfectly elastic collision when it reaches the vertical barrier on the right side of the slider $b$)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an inclined straight track AB, and the small block a slides down along the inclined plane from A to B; B, C, and D form a smooth circular arc track with radius R, C is the lowest point of the circular arc, the dashed line in the figure marks the center O1, B and D are symmetric near the vertical radius, and the height of D relative to C is R(1-cosθ). After D is connected a section of rough straight track DE with inclination angle θ and length L; after E is connected a smooth circular tube EF with radius R and central angle θ, the right side of F is aligned with the horizontal plane and the upper surface of skateboard b, and the right end of the skateboard has a vertical baffle. Reasoning: Take point C as the zero potential energy plane. 1) The whole path from A to C is smooth, and mechanical energy is conserved, so v_C^2=2gh=2×10×0.8=16 m^2/s^2. At point C, the centripetal direction is vertically upward, and there is N-mg=m v_C^2/R. Substituting m=0.5 kg, R=1 m gives N=0.5×10+0.5×16/1=5+8=13 N. 2) The height of point D is y_D=R(1-cosθ)=1×(1-0.8)=0.2 m. A to D is smooth, so the kinetic energy at point D is E_kD=mg(h-y_D)=0.5×10×(0.8-0.2)=3 J. When the block moves upward along the rough inclined plane DE, for each forward distance s it needs to overcome the component of gravity and friction to do work: W=(mg sinθ+μ1 mg cosθ)s. Substituting numerical values, mg sinθ=5×0.6=3 N, μ1 mg cosθ=0.75×5×0.8=3 N, therefore the total resistance is 6 N. Let 3=6s, obtaining s=0.5 m, and s<L=1.25 m, so the total distance the block moves on DE is 0.5 m. 3) When h=2.15 m, according to the height relationship in the problem figure and the given method, the height increment of point F relative to point C is 2R(1-cosθ)+L sinθ, and the friction loss on DE corresponds to the height term μ1 L cosθ. Thus v_F^2=2g[h-(2R(1-cosθ)+L sinθ)-μ1 L cosθ]. Substituting R=1, cosθ=0.8, sinθ=0.6, L=1.25, μ1=0.75 gives 2R(1-cosθ)=0.4, L sinθ=0.75, μ1Lcosθ=0.75, so the quantity in brackets is 2.15-0.4-0.75-0.75=0.25, hence v_F^2=20×0.25=5. a and b have equal masses, the horizontal plane of the skateboard is smooth, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the two is μ2=0.25. According to the given method, without the baffle, the relative sliding stopping distance is d0=v_F^2/(4μ2g)=5/(4×0.25×10)=0.5 m. Because the vertical baffle at the right end can make the small block undergo a completely elastic collision and move relatively in the reverse direction, the required minimum skateboard length is half of this relative stopping distance: l=d0/2=0.25 m.
